teachingQuestion: How is supplier assurance maintained after selection?
focalInsight: Supply-chain assurance begins before purchase and continues through delivery, operation, change, monitoring, and exit.
title: Supplier assurance across the dependency lifecycle
caption: Evidence collected at selection must be supplemented by operating controls and reassessment when the dependency changes.

nodes.label: Set enforceable requirements
nodes.detail: Minimum controls, SLAs, notice, audit, exit

nodes.label: Exit or recover
nodes.detail: Transition, revoke access, preserve required evidence

altSummary: A six-stage supplier lifecycle moves from defining criticality to assessment, contractual requirements, operation, monitoring, reassessment, and controlled exit.
textFallback: Define dependency criticality and required assurance. Assess the supplier, product, provenance, and dependencies. Put minimum requirements, service levels, notification, evidence, and exit terms into enforceable agreements. Operate with controlled access and evidence. Monitor changes and reassess. Transition or exit in a way that revokes access and maintains required evidence.
